user.title: SecuraCV Setup
user.description: Choose how to connect to your SecuraCV devices. Automatic is right for almost everyone: it detects what's installed and configures itself with no further questions.

data_description.setup_mode: Automatic probes for a running witness kernel (the SecuraCV app, or a sidecar announcing itself on MQTT) and enables MQTT for Canary devices. Pick a manual mode only if you need a non-default URL or topic prefix.

confirm.title: Add SecuraCV
confirm.description: Canary devices are publishing on the MQTT prefix `{prefix}`. Nothing else is needed — submit to add them to Home Assistant.

hassio_confirm.title: Add SecuraCV
hassio_confirm.description: The SecuraCV app announced its witness kernel. Submit to connect — nothing to type. Frigate events appear as sealed witness events within a minute of the next detection.

announce_confirm.title: Add the SecuraCV sidecar
announce_confirm.description: A SecuraCV sidecar announced its witness kernel `{device_id}` (kernel {kernel_version}). Its key fingerprint is `{fingerprint}` — the same eight characters `docker exec securacv pair` prints. Submit to pair; the next step asks for the 6-digit code and confirms the kernel URL ({url}).

pair.title: Pair with the SecuraCV sidecar
pair.description: On the Docker host run `docker exec securacv pair` and enter the 6-digit code it prints (valid 10 minutes). The kernel key fingerprint it prints beside the code must read `{fingerprint}` (kernel `{device_id}`). Home Assistant keeps its own paired key afterwards; revoke it any time with `docker exec securacv unpair` followed by the token id (`unpair` alone lists them).

data_description.url: Where Home Assistant reaches the sidecar's event API, usually http://DOCKER-HOST:8799 with the Docker host's LAN address in place of DOCKER-HOST. Pre-filled from the announcement or your MQTT broker's address — correct it if the sidecar runs elsewhere.
data_description.pairing_code: The 6 digits `pair` printed. Each code is single-use and burns after five wrong tries.

token_file.title: Witness Kernel token file
token_file.description: This kernel hands out its rotating token through a file Home Assistant can read (the app writes /config/api_token). Enter the kernel URL and the token file path, or a static token for a kernel whose file Home Assistant cannot read.

data_description.url: URL of the Privacy Witness Kernel Event API
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file; re-read automatically when the token rotates (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: Bearer token pasted from the kernel's api_token file — goes stale within 10 minutes unless a token file is also set
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: The prefix the kernel's MQTT bridge publishes under (default: witness)
data_description.adapter_stats_url: Read-only adapter_host stats endpoint, e.g. http://adapter-host:8799 — surfaces per-adapter health as a diagnostic sensor.

mqtt_config.title: MQTT Configuration
mqtt_config.description:
Configure MQTT for Canary device auto-discovery.

Canary devices publish to topics under this prefix. Devices will appear automatically in Home Assistant.

data_description.mqtt_prefix: MQTT topic prefix for Canary devices (default: securacv)

kernel.title: Witness Kernel Connection
kernel.description:
Enter the connection details for your SecuraCV Privacy Witness Kernel.

The kernel runs as a Home Assistant app, Docker container, or standalone service. The kernel rotates its API token every 10 minutes, so prefer the token file (the app writes it to /config/api_token); use a static token only for kernels whose token file Home Assistant cannot read. A Docker sidecar is better added through its announcement (Settings → Devices & Services → SecuraCV discovered), which pairs with a 6-digit code instead.

data_description.url: URL of the Privacy Witness Kernel Event API (e.g., http://d0491a67-privacy-witness-kernel:8799 for the app)
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file; re-read automatically when the token rotates (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: Bearer token pasted from the kernel's api_token file — goes stale within 10 minutes unless a token file is also set
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: The prefix the kernel's MQTT bridge publishes under (default: witness)
data_description.adapter_stats_url: Read-only adapter_host stats endpoint, e.g. http://adapter-host:8799 — surfaces per-adapter health as a diagnostic sensor.

both.title: MQTT + Kernel Connection
both.description: Configure both MQTT for Canary devices and HTTP for the Witness Kernel. The kernel rotates its API token every 10 minutes, so prefer the token file (the app writes it to /config/api_token).

data_description.url: URL of the Privacy Witness Kernel Event API
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file; re-read automatically when the token rotates (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: Bearer token pasted from the kernel's api_token file — goes stale within 10 minutes unless a token file is also set
data_description.mqtt_prefix: MQTT topic prefix for Canary devices (default: securacv)
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: The prefix the kernel's MQTT bridge publishes under (default: witness)
data_description.adapter_stats_url: Read-only adapter_host stats endpoint, e.g. http://adapter-host:8799 — surfaces per-adapter health as a diagnostic sensor.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate SecuraCV
reauth_confirm.description: The witness kernel rejected Home Assistant's credential. For a paired sidecar, run `docker exec securacv pair` on the Docker host and enter the new 6-digit code; for the app, check the token file path. The entry stays bound to the same kernel (fingerprint `{fingerprint}`).

data_description.url: Where Home Assistant reaches the kernel's event API.
data_description.pairing_code: The 6 digits `pair` printed; single-use, valid 10 minutes.
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: A pasted capability token, for kernels whose file Home Assistant cannot read.
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: The prefix the kernel's MQTT bridge publishes under (default: witness)

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure SecuraCV
reconfigure.description: Change where Home Assistant reaches this witness kernel, how it authenticates, or the prefix its MQTT bridge publishes under. The entry stays bound to the same kernel (fingerprint `{fingerprint}`); a different kernel is a new entry.

data_description.url: Where Home Assistant reaches the kernel's event API.
data_description.pairing_code: For a paired sidecar: a fresh code from `docker exec securacv pair`.
data_description.token_file: Path to the kernel's rotating token file (default: /config/api_token)
data_description.token: A pasted capability token, for kernels whose file Home Assistant cannot read.
data_description.mqtt_topic_prefix: The prefix the kernel's MQTT bridge publishes under (default: witness)

error.cannot_connect: Cannot connect to the Privacy Witness Kernel. Check the URL and ensure the kernel is running.
error.invalid_auth: Invalid API token. Check the token file path, or re-read the token from the kernel's api_token file.
error.token_required: Provide an API token file path or a static token (the token file is recommended — the kernel rotates the token every 10 minutes).
error.invalid_pairing_code: The code was not accepted. Run `docker exec securacv pair` again and enter the new code within 10 minutes.
error.paired_token_limit: The kernel already holds its limit of 32 paired tokens, so nothing was paired and this code is still valid. On the Docker host run `docker exec securacv unpair` to list them, revoke one with `docker exec securacv unpair` followed by its id, then submit the same code again.
error.kernel_identity_unavailable: The kernel answered but has no identity endpoint. Update the SecuraCV app or sidecar, then try again.
error.invalid_url: Enter the kernel URL with its scheme, like http://192.168.1.20:8799.

abort.already_configured: This SecuraCV system is already configured.
abort.already_in_progress: Configuration flow is already in progress.
abort.invalid_discovery_info: The discovery announcement was missing its connection details.
abort.not_securacv_device: This MQTT message is not a SecuraCV device announcement.
abort.announce_signature_invalid: The kernel announcement is not signed by the key Home Assistant pinned for that kernel, so it was ignored. If the kernel was reinstalled, resolve the key change under Settings → Repairs.
abort.announce_key_mismatch: The kernel's keys disagree: fingerprint `{received_fingerprint}` was received where `{pinned_fingerprint}` was expected. Nothing was changed. Compare both with the kernel's own printout (`docker exec securacv pair`, the app's panel, or `doctor`) before trying again.
abort.wrong_kernel: That is a different witness kernel. Add it as a new entry instead of moving this one.
abort.cannot_connect: The announced witness kernel could not be identified yet; it will be offered again on the app's next start.

create_entry.no_kernel_found:
No witness kernel is running yet. SecuraCV is set up and will connect by itself when one appears.

On Home Assistant OS: [add the SecuraCV app repository]({addon_repo_url}) and install SecuraCV from the App Store. Running Frigate under Docker? [Follow the quickstart]({docker_quickstart_url}). Only Canary devices? Nothing to do — they appear as they report.
create_entry.no_kernel_found_no_mqtt:
No witness kernel is running yet, and Home Assistant's MQTT integration is not set up; a sidecar can only be discovered once Home Assistant and the sidecar share a broker. SecuraCV is set up and connects by itself once that is in place.

On Home Assistant OS: [add the SecuraCV app repository]({addon_repo_url}) and install SecuraCV from the App Store. Running Frigate under Docker? [Follow the quickstart]({docker_quickstart_url}) and add the MQTT integration pointing at the same broker. Only Canary devices? Add the MQTT integration — they appear as they report.

mqtt_subscribe_failed.title: SecuraCV can't subscribe to MQTT

no_kernel_found.title: No SecuraCV witness kernel found
no_kernel_found.description:
SecuraCV is set up for Canary devices only; no witness kernel is sealing Frigate events yet. It connects by itself when one appears.

On Home Assistant OS: [add the SecuraCV app repository]({addon_repo_url}) and install SecuraCV from the App Store. Running Frigate under Docker? [Follow the quickstart]({docker_quickstart_url}) and pair the sidecar from the card that appears here. Only Canary devices? Dismiss this — there is nothing to do.

kernel_unreachable.title: SecuraCV can't reach the witness kernel
kernel_unreachable.description: Home Assistant has not been able to reach the witness kernel at {url} for 15 minutes. Check that the SecuraCV app or sidecar is running, and that the URL is right (Settings > Devices & Services > SecuraCV > Reconfigure). This clears itself as soon as the kernel answers again.

confirm.title: Confirm the kernel's new key
confirm.description:
The witness kernel at {url} now serves the key with fingerprint `{received_fingerprint}`; Home Assistant pinned `{pinned_fingerprint}`. This happens after a restore to new hardware or a reinstalled app or sidecar — or when something else answers at that address. Until you confirm the new key, kernel events show a key mismatch and are never shown as verified.

Before submitting, compare `{received_fingerprint}` with what the kernel itself prints: `docker exec securacv pair`, the app's panel, or `doctor`. Submit only if they match. The previous key stays recorded in the entry so earlier sealed logs remain attributable; the integration reloads and verifies against the new key.

abort.no_received_key: This issue carries no key to confirm; it is raised again with the key on the next check.

storage_replace.title: The witness kernel's storage should be replaced
storage_replace.description: The kernel reports its storage at {wear_pct}% estimated wear or failing writes. Export your evidence first (the Export evidence button or the securacv.export_evidence action), then replace the card or disk; the sealed log lives in the app's or sidecar's data directory and moves with it.

entities_migrated.title: SecuraCV replaced the app's pwk_* entities
entities_migrated.description:
Now that the SecuraCV integration manages this witness kernel, the entities the app published through MQTT discovery have been withdrawn and replaced:

- `sensor.pwk_last_event` → `sensor.securacv_last_event`
- `sensor.pwk_daily_digest` → `sensor.securacv_daily_digest`
- `binary_sensor.pwk_chain_problem` → `binary_sensor.securacv_chain_valid` (on means the chain is intact)
- `button.pwk_verify_now` → `button.securacv_verify_now`
- the per-zone sensors → one `event.securacv_` entity per camera, named after it (`event.securacv_front_door`, say)

Update automations and dashboards that referenced the old ids; the SecuraCV dashboard strategy already uses the new ones. Dismiss this notice when done.

init.title: Device key management
init.description: Pin, rotate, or unpin a Canary device's Ed25519 public key. Read the key off the device, not over MQTT: a canary-wap shows it on its /enroll page, the firmware/canary build and canary-vision print it on USB serial (`j`), and a canary-sense or canary-sentinel on a firmware release after 2.4.15 prints it once at boot on its serial console, as the `Ed25519 pubkey` line (2.4.15 and older print only the fingerprint). A canary-display has no key to pin.

pin.title: Pin device pubkey
pin.description: Paste the device_id and the full 64-character Ed25519 pubkey hex, read off the device: the /enroll page on a canary-wap, the USB serial `j` output on the firmware/canary build or canary-vision, or, on a canary-sense or canary-sentinel running a firmware release after 2.4.15, the `Ed25519 pubkey` line it prints on its serial console at boot, with the `Device ID` line later in the same log.

rotate.title: Rotate pinned key
rotate.description: Replace the existing pin with a new pubkey. The previous key is retained in the audit trail. The mismatch notification for this device (if any) is cleared.

unpin.title: Unpin device
unpin.description: Drop the device's pin. The next publish will TOFU-pin to whatever pubkey arrives.

settings.title: Evidence exports
settings.description: How many evidence packs to keep under the Home Assistant configuration directory (securacv/evidence). When a new export exceeds the limit, the oldest pack is removed and the export notification says so.

error.invalid_pubkey_hex: Public key must be exactly 64 hex characters (0-9, a-f, either case), with no spaces or trailing dots.
error.device_not_pinned: No pin exists for this device_id.
error.trust_store_unavailable: The trust store isn't loaded for this entry — try reloading the integration.

no_loaded_entry.message: SecuraCV has no loaded entry, so nothing is running its watches. Enable or reload the integration to use them.

watches_unreadable.message: SecuraCV could not read its stored watches (the log has the reason), so its watches are not available. Reload the integration to try again.

not_loaded_yet.message: SecuraCV is not loaded yet, so its watches are not available. Try again once the integration has started.

duration_unreadable.message: Can't tell how long {duration} is. Give it in days, weeks, months, seasons or years ("two weeks", "10 days"), or leave it out for {default_days} days.

subject_empty.message: Say what to keep an eye on: subject is empty.

watch_limit_reached.message: Already running {count} watches, which is as many as the hub keeps. End one with securacv.end_watch first.

watch_ref_empty.message: Say which watch to end: its id or its label.

watch_not_found.message: No watch is called {watch}. securacv.list_watches names the ones running.

watch_ambiguous.message: {watch} names {count} watches ({ids}); end it by id.

no_kernel_entry.message: No SecuraCV entry with a witness kernel is loaded, so there is no sealed log to verify or export. Add the SecuraCV app or sidecar first.

kernel_entry_ambiguous.message: {count} SecuraCV entries have a witness kernel; say which one with entry_id.

entry_not_loaded.message: SecuraCV entry {entry_id} is not loaded or has no witness kernel.

window_out_of_range.message: window_hours is {window_hours}; give a whole number of hours from {min_hours} to {max_hours}.

kernel_unreachable.message: The witness kernel did not answer. Check that the SecuraCV app or sidecar is running, then try again.

kernel_auth_failed.message: The witness kernel rejected Home Assistant's credential. Re-authenticate the SecuraCV entry under Settings → Devices & services.

kernel_bad_response.message: The witness kernel answered with something other than the sealed log or the evidence bundle: {detail}.

export_write_failed.message: The evidence pack could not be written under the configuration directory: {detail}.

start_watch.name: Start a watch
start_watch.description: Starts a bounded, self-expiring watch on something the fleet already senses. Adds attention only: it cannot arm, disarm or unseal anything, and it never turns on new sensing. Returns the watch, including the id that End a watch takes.

subject.name: Subject
subject.description: What to keep an eye on, the way you would say it. A Canary's name binds the watch to that device's witness events; anything else is accepted but stays unfed until something in the fleet reports it.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long, in days, weeks, months, seasons or years: "two weeks", "10 days", "a month". A duration with none of those units ("48 hours") is refused, not guessed. 14 days if left out; never longer than a year.

concern.name: Concern
concern.description: What to tell you about. Left out, it is read off the subject's wording ("if it stops reporting"), or it is "if anything changes".

end_watch.name: End a watch
end_watch.description: Ends a watch early and removes it. Name it by its id (from Start a watch or List watches) or by its label; a label two watches share is refused rather than guessed. The early end is announced like an expiry. Returns the watch as it ended.

watch.name: Watch
watch.description: The watch's id, or its label as you said it.

list_watches.name: List watches
list_watches.description: Returns the watches currently running, each with its state, what it is bound to and how many days it has left. Response only.

verify.name: Verify the witness chain
verify.description: Walks the kernel's sealed log now and checks every entry's hash link and Ed25519 signature against the key Home Assistant pinned when it connected. Only this walk earns an event its "Verified" mark; the kernel's own self-check never does. Returns the verdict, how many new entries verified and the bucket the walk ran in.

entry_id.name: Kernel
entry_id.description: Which SecuraCV entry to verify, when more than one has a witness kernel. The only one if left out.

export_evidence.name: Export evidence
export_evidence.description: Downloads the kernel's signed evidence bundle for the last N hours and writes ONE zip under the configuration directory (securacv/evidence, readable by Home Assistant only): the bundle verbatim, the offline viewer, a README for the recipient and the witness key. A persistent notification carries a download link valid 24 hours; the pack is also under Media → SecuraCV evidence. Nothing is added to, removed from or re-serialized in the bundle.

window_hours.name: Window
window_hours.description: How far back, in whole hours (1–720). 24 if left out.

entry_id.name: Kernel
entry_id.description: Which SecuraCV entry to export from, when more than one has a witness kernel. The only one if left out.
